s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital swelling with vision deterioration and proptosis
salient_findings: Left fronto-orbital swelling of 10 years’ duration
Progressive deterioration of vision in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Left fronto-orbital swelling for 10 years
Progressive vision deterioration in the left eye over 1.5 years
Proptosis with inferior and medial displacement of the left globe
No history of endocrine abnormalities
Heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof on MRI
Expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit on CT
Lesion involves the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing
Vision in the left eye is barely perceptible to hand movements near the face

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Long-standing orbital swelling and lytic bony lesion

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of the sphenoid wing and dural-based lesion

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Expansive lytic bony lesion with possible soft tissue component

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic bony lesion with possible fluid-fluid levels on imaging

shortlist.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital roof involvement with mixed lytic and sclerotic features

raw.rationale: The long duration of symptoms (10 years) and the presence of a heterogeneous enhancing mass with an expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital roof, frontal bone, and sphenoid wing are consistent with fibrous dysplasia, which is known for its slow growth and potential to cause progressive bone deformation and vision impairment.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: While meningioma could explain some of the findings, the long history and specific bone involvement pattern is more typical of fibrous dysplasia

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are typically more aggressive and have a different radiographic appearance

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are usually more fluid-filled and expansile, with a different clinical presentation

rejected.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: Fibro-osseous lesion is a broader category that includes fibrous dysplasia, but the specific details provided point more directly to fibrous dysplasia
